key_insight: Dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can reduce coating defects on Q235 steel, with service humidity also influencing wear performance.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and sliding wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links higher porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance values or humidity ranges, limiting quantitative comparisons and service-condition guidance.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
